Definition: Whether the system enables individuals to authenticate themselves or their documents digitally through electronic verification
Comments: E-Houwiya provides full digital authentication functionality: two-factor authentication (login/password + SMS OTP), X.509 PKI certificates and cryptographic keys, qualified digital signatures legally equivalent to handwritten signatures, and single sign-on (SSO) access to government portals. The 2024 biometric CIN law also includes an authentication certificate on the chip (Article 2 of Organic Law 2024-22).

Definition: Whether authentication is possible through a centralized government portal or digital gateway
Comments: E-Houwiya serves as the centralized SSO for Tunisian government portals including E-Bawaba (official e-government portal), E-CNAM (national health insurance), E-People, E-CNSS (social security), Madrassati (education), and E-Barid (official government email). Citizens can access thousands of online administrative services using E-Houwiya authentication.

Definition: Whether individuals can view their data held in the ID database and see how it has been accessed
Comments: Tunisian law provides individuals the right to access their personal data. Organic Law 2004-63 (Art. 32) grants the right to consult, correct, rectify, update, or erase personal data. The 2024 biometric CIN law (Art. 2 bis) explicitly grants the CIN holder access to their encrypted chip data, with audit trails of all accesses. The RIUC citizen portal was planned to allow citizens to view their data and access history per LPDP requirements.

Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: E-Houwiya is integrated with the banking sector for remote onboarding and KYC compliance, following Central Bank of Tunisia KYC regulations published February 28, 2025. The CIN is the primary KYC document under Organic Law 2015-26 (AML/CFT). Uqudo has partnered with Tunisian entities to provide AI/biometric KYC verification for passports and CINs. E-Houwiya enables remote KYC for banking and fintech services.

Definition: Whether the ID authority and system are subject to general oversight of the courts and judicial review
Value Name: Yes, but not specific to ID
Comments: Judicial oversight of the ID system is indirect. INPDP decisions can be appealed to the Tunis Court of Appeal and further to the Court of Cassation (per Organic Law 2004-63). There is no ID-specific judicial oversight mechanism; courts provide general oversight through the appeals process. The 2024 Biometric ID law requires INPDP consultation for implementing decrees. No dedicated ID tribunal or specialized judicial body exists.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Civil registration (Madania system) is partially integrated with the national ID system. The RIUC was initialized from Madania + CIN data and permanent links for real-time birth/death updates were planned. CIN enrollment requires a birth extract from Madania. The World Bank diagnostic notes the RIUC system links CR and CIN but full real-time interoperability has not been completed. IS social identifier queries Madania via 8 attributes. Full integration is underway but not yet complete.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Data sharing rules exist but are only partially available/enforced. Organic Law 2004-63 requires INPDP authorization for data sharing and prohibits transfer abroad without authorization. The 2024 biometric ID law requires encrypted chip access by authorized agencies only (Ministry of Interior agents, customs, with audit trails). However, civil society organizations documented cases where the E-Houwiya and subsidy platforms bypassed INPDP consultation requirements, indicating partial compliance.

Definition: Whether specific regulation or policy addresses digital ID beyond general identification legislation
Comments: Organic Law No. 2024-22 (March 11, 2024) specifically governs the biometric national identity card with electronic chip, digital authentication certificates, and electronic signatures. The E-Houwiya system operates under a specific legal framework establishing it as legally equivalent to face-to-face identification. Decree-Law 2023-17 regulates cybersecurity for digital systems including mandatory audits.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: Organic Law No. 2004-63 (July 27, 2004) on the Protection of Personal Data is in force. It establishes data subject rights (access, rectification, opposition), requires prior declaration/authorization for processing, mandates consent, and includes criminal sanctions. Critics note it is outdated and a new GDPR-aligned law has been drafted since 2018 but not yet enacted as of 2025.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Instance Nationale de Protection des Données à Caractère Personnel (INPDP) was established by Decree No. 2007-3003 under Organic Law 2004-63. It oversees data processing registrations/authorizations, handles complaints, issues decisions, and its decisions can be appealed to the Tunis Court of Appeal. INPDP must be consulted on legislation affecting personal data (though this was bypassed for E-Houwiya and the subsidy platform, raising civil society concerns).

Definition: Whether the digital ID credential serves as legal proof of an individual's identity as codified in law
Comments: The CIN is the sole legal document certifying individual identity in Tunisia; it is required for all administrative procedures, mandatory by law for citizens 18+. The E-Houwiya digital signature is legally valid and equivalent to a handwritten signature. Organic Law 2024-22 confirms the CIN as a 'document personnel certifiant l'identité de son titulaire.' Digital ID (E-Houwiya) is legally recognized for online transactions.

Definition: Whether formal legislation (act, law, regulation) governs digital identity including identification acts, digital ID laws, or equivalent legislation
Comments: Tunisia has a comprehensive legal framework for ID: Law 1993-27 on the CIN (amended by Organic Law 2024-22 introducing biometric CIN); Organic Law 2004-63 on Personal Data Protection; Decree 2007-3003 establishing the INPDP; the 2022 Digital Code framework; Decree-Law 2023-17 on cybersecurity; and Constitutional Article 24 guaranteeing privacy. E-Houwiya digital signatures are legally valid per existing electronic transaction law.

Definition: Whether the system and the production of credentials can be managed, maintained and developed by in-country technical staff (as opposed to foreign vendors)
Comments: All core ID systems are maintained by Tunisian government entities: Madania CR system by Ministry of Local Affairs (MALE) via the National Informatics Center (CNI); CIN system by Ministry of Interior (Technical Police); E-Houwiya by Ministry of Communication Technologies and its affiliated entities (National Digital Certification Agency, CNI, local telecom operators); RIUC under MALE/MTCEN. E-Houwiya was developed with Estonian eGA advisory support (MOU 2022) but operated domestically.

Definition: Whether the Ministry of Finance has oversight of the financing and development of the digital ID system
Comments: The Ministry of Finance participates in the biometric ID steering committee (noted in April 2024 ministerial session chaired by PM Hachani, attended by Minister of Finance Sihem Nemsia Boughdiri alongside ministers of Interior, Communication Technologies, and Economy). However, the Ministry of Finance does not have primary oversight of the digital ID system; oversight is primarily with the Ministry of Interior (CIN) and Ministry of Communication Technologies (E-Houwiya).

Definition: Whether the ongoing management, maintenance and development of the ID system can be funded by sustainable domestic resources
Comments: Tunisia's ID systems are primarily domestically financed. The CIN system is funded through the Ministry of Interior budget; the Madania civil registration system is funded via local government and MALE. The E-Houwiya system is operated by the Ministry of Communication Technologies and affiliated state entities (CNI, National Digital Certification Agency, telecom operators). The World Bank provided a diagnostic (2020) and advisory support, and Estonian eGA provided technical advisory (MOU 2022), but operational funding is domestic.

Definition: Whether the system collects biometric data and which modalities are collected (fingerprints, facial image, iris scans)
Comments: The existing CIN (pre-2024) collects a digitized thumbprint image (inked, printed on card back) but no electronic biometric template. Organic Law No. 2024-22 (March 2024) legislated a new biometric CIN requiring fingerprints stored on an electronic chip; however, as of late 2025 physical rollout had not occurred. RIUC system uses only demographic deduplication (no biometrics). Current live system = fingerprints only (image-based), not full digital biometric database.

Definition: Whether identity records are stored in electronic/digital format versus paper-based records
Comments: All major ID databases are fully digital. The Madania civil registration system (SQL Server, fully operational since April 2005) centralizes all civil registration across 350 municipalities. The CIN database is fully electronic (Cobol/VSE-CICS system). The RIUC holds 15 million records in a centralized Oracle database. Social protection IS database uses Oracle 12c. Paper registers are also maintained for legal validity of civil status but all administration is digital.

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: Tunisia operates two foundational digital ID systems fully deployed nationwide: the CIN (Carte d'Identité Nationale, paper card with digital database, mandatory for citizens 18+) and the E-Houwiya mobile digital identity launched August 2022 covering all Tunisian citizens. A biometric CIN was legislated (Organic Law 2024-22) and rollout was planned for H1 2025. The existing systems are digitally managed and nationally deployed.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: Tunisia's E-Houwiya functions as SSO across multiple government portals (E-Bawaba, E-CNAM, E-People, E-CNSS, Madrassati). The RIUC (Registre de l'Identifiant Unique du Citoyen) was being implemented as a central dictionary linking sectoral identifiers across agencies via TunXRoad platform. However, the World Bank diagnostic noted low integration and interoperability between systems in 2020, partially improved with IS social identifier linking social protection funds.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: The CIN is the primary accepted KYC document for banking (Organic Law 2015-26; Central Bank circulars). E-Houwiya is accepted (not mandatory) for remote banking onboarding and KYC per Central Bank of Tunisia regulations published February 28, 2025. Banking does not legally mandate E-Houwiya specifically; the physical CIN remains the primary mandatory document. E-Houwiya integration with banking is expanding but optional.

Definition: Whether credentials are issued free of charge
Comments: The physical CIN requires payment of a fiscal stamp (timbre fiscal) for issuance/renewal. The initial CIN costs approximately 3 Tunisian dinars and replacement costs 25 dinars. However, the E-Houwiya digital ID is explicitly free of charge: 'The E-Houwiya ID is free of charge, because to encourage adoption of digital IDs, the cost of issuing it should be equal or less than the cost of issuing the physical ID card.' There is a cost for the physical credential.

Definition: Whether the digital ID is recognized or interoperable across borders through regional agreements or travel documents
Value Name: Recognized in some regional contexts (e.g., ECOWAS travel)
Comments: Tunisia's CIN is recognized for travel within some regional contexts; Tunisians can travel to some Maghreb countries (Algeria, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco) using the CIN instead of a passport. The biometric ID/passport laws (Organic Laws 2024-22/23) explicitly align with ICAO recommendations to enhance cross-border recognition. There is no formal digital ID interoperability framework with other countries; recognition is limited to some regional travel agreements.

Definition: Age in years at which an individual becomes eligible to register for digital ID
Comments: Under Organic Law 2024-22 (March 2024), the CIN is mandatory for Tunisian nationals aged 15 and over. Exceptionally, it can be issued to those aged 12-15 with parental consent. The E-Houwiya digital ID requires holding a physical CIN (minimum age 18). Previous law required CIN from age 18. The new minimum mandatory age of 15 (with option from 12) falls in the '>17' bracket based on actual mandatory requirement.

Definition: Whether registration for digital ID is mandatory, optional, or mandatory for specific groups
Comments: CIN enrollment is mandatory for all Tunisian nationals aged 15 and over under Organic Law 2024-22 (previously 18+). The E-Houwiya digital ID is optional (no legal obligation to possess it as of 2025, per the system architect). Civil registration (birth) is mandatory for all citizens. The physical CIN is mandatory for all eligible citizens; digital ID (E-Houwiya) is optional.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for accessing public healthcare services
Comments: The CIN is required for healthcare access in Tunisia. Free care cards and reduced-price healthcare cards require CIN copies from all family members over 18. The CNAM (national health insurance) digital card distribution began in 2019. Access to public health establishments and CNAM services requires identity verification via CIN. E-Houwiya serves as SSO for E-CNAM portal. The CIN is mandatory for healthcare access.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Non-Tunisian residents are required to carry a residence card (carte de résidence) issued by the Ministry of Interior, usable for KYC purposes. The CIN is for Tunisian nationals only. The E-Houwiya digital ID is explicitly limited to Tunisian nationals (aged 18+ holding a CIN). The RIUC system covers Tunisian nationals only. Non-nationals have some access to an identity credential (residence card) but not the national digital ID system.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Civil registration (Madania) covers 99% of the population. The CIN covers approximately 90% of adults aged 18+ (World Bank estimate). The RIUC holds records for 15 million individuals. E-Houwiya had 200,000 subscribers as of March 2025 (lower digital ID coverage). The foundational ID coverage (civil register + CIN combined) exceeds 89% of the total population.

Definition: Whether ID system undergoes regular security audits, penetration testing, or vulnerability assessments
Comments: Decree-Law 2023-17 on cybersecurity mandates annual IT security audits for entities processing personal data, with reporting to the National Cybersecurity Agency (ANCS). The Ministry of Communication Technologies issued decisions on procedures for granting a 'secure' label to software/equipment (September 2023). Mandatory periodic security audits of information systems are required. However, civil society notes that transparency of security reviews for E-Houwiya is limited.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: SIM card registration in Tunisia requires a national ID (CIN) or passport, and is mandatory under telecommunications legislation. In September 2024, the Ministry of Communication Technologies enforced stricter regulations requiring telecom operators to deactivate unregistered SIMs and verify all subscribers with official identification. Operators must maintain databases of subscriber identities accessible to authorities.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for registering for social assistance programs and accessing social services
Comments: The CIN is mandatory for access to social services in Tunisia. The Ministry of Social Affairs requires CIN copies from all family members over 18 for eligibility assessment for social programs (Amen social program, free healthcare cards). The World Bank diagnostic confirms all functional ID systems require CIN as proof of identity for transactions such as collecting social security payments. No administrative procedure can be completed without presenting the CIN.
